subject: radiology
title: Radiation safety: ALARA in practice

steps.tx: Radiation dose builds silently during fluoroscopy, so every operator works to keep exposure low for patient and staff. The **ALARA principle** means the team keeps each exposure as low as reasonably achievable in daily practice. Staff shorten beam time, increase distance from the source, and use shielding whenever the case allows. A **pulsed fluoroscopy** setting with last image hold cuts dose while the operator still sees enough guidance. Tight **collimation** narrows the beam to the target area, and the team logs the **dose area product** for every case carefully.
steps.say: Radiation dose builds silently during screening so every operator works to keep exposure low always. The guiding principle means the team keeps each exposure as low as reasonably achievable daily. Staff shorten beam time and increase distance and use shielding whenever the case allows it. A pulsed setting with last image hold cuts dose while the operator still sees enough guidance. Tight narrowing limits the beam to the target and the team logs the dose for every case.

steps.tx: Every person in the lab needs personal shielding during each fluoroscopy case without exception. A **lead apron with thyroid collar** guards the torso and the thyroid gland against scattered radiation effectively. A ceiling suspended screen and a table skirt block scatter before the rays reach the operator body. Each operator wears a **dosimeter badge** at the collar outside the lead so the badge tracks true exposure. An operator who becomes pregnant declares the pregnancy early so the team can plan **fetal dose** limits and duties safely.
steps.say: Every person in the lab needs personal shielding during each screening case without any exception. A lead apron with a neck collar guards the torso and the thyroid gland against scatter. A ceiling screen and a table skirt block scatter before the rays reach the operator. Each operator wears a badge at the collar outside the lead so the badge tracks true exposure. An operator who becomes pregnant declares the pregnancy early so the team can plan safe duties.

steps.tx: High skin dose can injure the patient, although severe injury remains uncommon in routine practice. The team watches the **skin dose** during long cases because a high dose predicts later skin damage. Redness and **hair loss** that appear weeks later mark a deterministic injury and the patient then needs specialist skin review. The operator lens also suffers over years, and **cataract** develops sooner when the operator works without lead glasses. The team screens for **pregnancy** before pelvic work so an unborn child avoids accidental exposure completely.

steps.tx: Radiation safety continues after the patient leaves the lab, because dose accumulates across a lifetime of studies. The hospital keeps a **dose registry** that follows high dose patients across every repeat procedure over years. Before a complex case, the consent discussion names the radiation risk frankly so the patient decides with full knowledge. Regular **audit with feedback** compares operators and the comparison drives doses down across the whole department. Each new staff member learns safe habits from the first day because **training** embeds the culture early and permanently.
